newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seeks to scrap withholding tax on new bonds.
newsitem.headline: Manila seeks to scrap withholding tax on new bonds.

text.p: The Philippines will work to exempt the soon-to-be-issued uncollateralised Brady bonds from the 20 percent withholding tax, finance secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Friday.
"The Philippines has informed JP Morgan that it expects to take appropriate action to render the new bonds exempt from Philippine withholding taxes," de Ocampo told reporters.
JP Morgan is the lead arranger for the Brady exchange offer.
De Ocampo said the department has the authority to give tax exempt status on government securities.
The Philippines has offered to exchange $1.9 billion of defaulted debt bonds into new uncollateralised bonds.
The invitation to exchange the Brady bonds began on September 2 and ended today. Acceptance of offers will be announced on September 20 and settlement done on October 7.
